details.llm_def: The word "ram" primarily means to rest, remain quiet, or stay. It also signifies being pleased, delighted, or rejoicing, often involving sexual intercourse. Additionally, it can denote playing or sporting. The term can causally mean to please or delight someone.

definitions.text: augment र inserted after the vowel अ of the root भ्रस्ज्, when the letterर् which is already present in भ्ररुज् (before अ) and the penultimate स् are dropped; the result is that the word भर्ज्, in short, becomes substituted in the place of भ्रस्ज्ः cf. भ्रस्जो रोपधयो रमन्यतरस्याम्P.VI. 4.47, and भ्रस्जो रोपधयोर्लोप आगमो रम् विधीयते as Bharadvajiya Varttika thereon

Ram's fat is utilized in the manufacturing of silver when mixed with fish fat and heated in a glass bottle according to Rasa Jala Nidhi, volume 1 [1]. Additionally, Ram meat is recommended in the diet for patients suffering from Udavarta and Anaha, as mentioned in Rasa Jala Nidhi, volume 4 [2].

definitions.text: {c1c} Ātmane-pada (ramate, but Paras. when preceded by vi, ā, pari and upa; reme, araṃsta, araṃsīt Par. raṃsyate, raṃtuṃ, rata,) 1 To be pleased or delighted, rejoice, be gratified; rahasi ramate [Māl. 3. 2],  [Ms. 2. 223]; [U. 2. 18.] --2 To rejoice at, be pleased with, take delight in, be fond of (with [instr.] or locative case.) lolāpāṃgairyadi na ramase locanairvaṃcito'si [Me. 27.]; vyajeṣṭa ṣaḍvargamaraṃsta nītau [Bk. 1. 2.] --3 To play, sport, dally, amuse oneself with; rājapriyāḥ kairaviṇyo ramaṃte madhupaiḥ saha [Bv. 1. 126] (where the next meaning is also hinted); [Bk. 6. 15], [Bk. 6.]67.] --4 To have sexual intercourse with; sā tatputreṇa saha ramate [H. 3.] --5 To remain, stay, pause. --6 To take rest, remain quiet. --7 To gladden, delight. --Causal. (ramayati-te) To please, delight, satisfy. --Desiderative. (riraṃsate) To wish to sport &c.;[Śi. 15. 88.]

definitions.text:
RAM, i. 1, [Ātm.] (in poetry also [Par.], [Man.] 2, 223), in the Veda also ii. 9, [Par.] 1. To rest, [Man.] 3, 251; to like to stay, [Hit.] ii. [d.] 128. 2. To be delighted, [Pañc.] i. [d.] 429; to rejoice, [Rām.] 2, 34, 50; [Vikr.] 19, 1 (raṃsyate bhavatā, impers. [pass.] You will be glad), 70, 21. 3. To rejoice at, with locative case., [Daśak.] in [Chr.] 181, 5 (to be in love); with [instr.], [MBh.] 3, 58. 4. To have sexual intercourse with ([instr.]), [Hit.] 66, 7. 5. To sport, [Bhaṭṭ.] 6, 15. [Ptcple.] of the [pf.] [pass.] rata. 1. Beloved, [Pañc.] v. [d.] 53. 2. Intent on, [Man.] 2, 235 (with locative case.); occupied, [Pañc.] 27, 9. 3. Inclined, [Pañc.] 203, 2. 4. Satisfied, [Pañc.] 228, 10. neuter gender. 1. Coition, copulation, [Pañc.] i. [d.] 224. 2. A private part. [Comp.] Deva-, adjective. devout, [Pañc.] 118, 22. Nirmāṇa-, masculine gender. the name of a class of deities, [MBh.] 13, 1372. Su-, I. adjective. 1. playing, playful. 2. compassionate, tender. II. neuter gender. 1. coition, [Hit.] iii. 27. 2. sexual intercourse, love, [Ṛt.] 6, 1. Vara-su-, adjective. very wanton, [Hit.] ii. [d.] 64. [Ptcple.] of the [fut.] [pass.] I. rantavya, To be rejoiced at, [Mṛcch.] 62, 22. II. ramaṇīya, Pleasing, agreeable, [Vikr.] 37, 10; [Hit.] iv. [d.] 73 (āpāta-, in the beginning); beautiful, [Vikr.] 65, 18 (viśeṣa-, most beautiful). III. ramya. 1. The same, [Ṛt.] 6, 2. 2. masculine gender. The champaca, Michelia Champaca. 3. feminine. yā. a. Night. b. The name of a river. 4. neuter gender. Semen virile. [Comp.] Nis-ātapatra-, adjective. needing no parasol, id est. cool, and therefore charming, a Karmadhāraya compound, [Vikr.] [d.] 73. Causal. ramaya, 1. To exhilarate, [MBh.] 2, 305. 
2. To be delighted, to rejoice, [MBh.] 3, 11379. -- With the [prep.] anu anu, anurata, 1. Fond of, attached to. 2. Beloved. -- With abhi abhi, To be delighted, to rejoice, [Rām.] 2, 27, 18. abhirata, 1. Intent upon, [Chr.] 14, 26. 2. Pleased with. 3. Engaged in, [Rām.] 3, 49, 39. 4. Practising. -- With ava ava, avarata, Stopped, ceased. [Comp.] An-, adjective. uninterrupted, [Vedāntas.] in [Chr.] 216, 21. °tam, [adv.] without stopping, [Pañc.] 93, 15; incessantly, [Pañc.] 145, 14. -- With ā ā, [Par.] 1. To repose, [Bhaṭṭ.] 3, 38. 2. To cease, [Man.] 2, 73. 3. To take pleasure, [Man.] 4, 175. anata, Ceased, [Kir.] 5, 6. -- With upā upa-ā, 1. To repose, [MBh.] 1, 6035. 2. To cease, [Ragh.] 16, 3 (Calc.). 3. To rejoice, to dally, [MBh.] 1, 4183. -- With upa upa, [Par.] [Ātm.] 1. To cease, [Chr.] 30, 39; with the [ptcple.] of the [pres.] in the sense of the infin., [Pañc.] 53, 19 (mṛgaśaśakādin vyāpādayan nopa rarāma, He did not cease killing deer, hares, etc.). 2. To desist from, with ablative case., [Daśak.] in [Chr.] 181, 12. uparata, 1. Stopped, ceased. 2. Having ceased, [Man.] 5, 66. 3. Having desisted from, [Bhaṭṭ.] 2, 35. 4. Dead, [Pañc.] 98, 3 (he breathed out his last). -- With vyupa vi-upa, vyuparata, Interrupted, stopped, [Mṛcch.] 1, 2. -- With ni ni, nirata, 1. Pleased, satisfied, [Man.] 3, 45. 2. Attached to (with locative case.), loving, [Utt. Rāmac.] 57, 5; faithful, [Rām.] 3, 48, 18. 3. Engaged in, practising, [Nal.] 6, 10 (a-hiṃsā-, benevolence). -- With pari pari, [Par.] To be delighted, [Bhaṭṭ.] 8, 53. -- With vi vi, 1. To cease, [Utt. Rāmac.] 17, 6; with the [ptcple.] of the [pres.] in the sense 
of the infin., [Pañc.] 93, 16. 2. To desist, [Man.] 4, 97. 3. To cease from, desist from (with ablative case.), [Vikr.] [d.] 39; [Pañc.] 161, 1. virata, Stopped, ceased, [Śiś.] 9, 12. [Comp.] A-, adjective. 1. uninterrupted, [Kir.] 5, 6. 2. eternal. -- With sam sam, To rejoice, [Bhaṭṭ.] 19, 30. -[Cf.] [O.H.G.] rāwa, ruowa (id est. *ram + van, confer, compare. accusative case. singular number. ruouun), rāwên (denomin.), resti, rastjan; [A.S.] rest, restan; [Greek:ἠρέμα, νω-λεμ + ής].

ra/mate ra/ma°ti ramṇāti [pp.] rate ([q.v.]) tr. stop, fix, settle; gladden, delight, enjoy (especially. carnally); intr. stop, rest, stay gladly with (locative case. or dative case.); delight in, be pleased with or to (locative case., [instr.], or Infinitive mood.); be happy or content; dally or have sexual intercourse with ([instr.] ±samam, saha, sākam, or sārdham). [C.] rama/yati or rāma/yati = [S.] [trans.] — anu Ātmane-pada stop (intr.), stay; [M.] find pleasure or delight. abhi [M.] stop, stay; delight in, be satisfied or pleased with (locative case. or [instr.] ±saha). upāva [M.] feel comfortable. ā Ātmane-pada stop, cease; take delight in (locative case.), enjoy carnally ([instr.] ±samam). upā Ātmane-pada ([M.]) rest, repose, desist from (ablative case.). vyupā & samā the same. upa Ātmane-pada stop (tr.); Ātmane-pada[M.] stop (intr.), rest, stay repose; cease from, renounce, resign (ablative case.). vyupa Ātmane-pada [M.] come to rest, cease, desist from (ablative case.). ni [M.] go to rest, cease, end. [C.] nirāmayati stop, check, restrain. pari Ātmane-pada take pleasure in, rejoice at (ablative case.). vi Ātmane-pada ([M.])
stop, cease, pause, rest; desist from (ablative case.), renounce, resign (ablative case. or [absol.]). [C.] viramayati or virāmayati bring to rest or to an end. — Cf. anurata, uparata ([add.]), nirata (to be placed after nirañjana), virata.

definitions.text: ram, cl. 1. A. (in poetry also P.) ramate (-ti), reme, raṃsyate, araṃsta (in the Veda also cl. 9. P. ramṇāti, &c.) rantum, (and with a preposition sometimes) ramitum, to stop, stay, calm, tranquillize, (in these senses cl. 9. P., Ved.); to rest, repose, remain quiet, take one's ease (cl. 1. A.); to remain, stay, pause; to like to stay or remain; to make happy, rejoice, please (cl. 1. P. and A.); to be pleased or delighted, to rejoice (cl. 1. A.); to be pleased with or rejoice at, take delight in (with loc. or inst. or with saha and inst.); to play or sport with, dally with (with inst. or with saha and inst., or with sārdham &c. and inst.); to have sexual intercourse with (with inst.), know carnally (with acc.); to couple (said of deer): Caus. ramayati (according to some also rāmayati), -yitum, Aor. arīramat (Ved. ramayāmakaḥ, Pāṇ. III. 1, 42), to cause to stay, stop Vedic or Veda.; to calm, tranquillize Vedic or Veda.; to delight, gratify, please, rejoice, amuse, give pleasure, cause (sexual) enjoyment; to cause to couple (said of deer); to be pleased or delighted, to rejoice: Desid. riraṃsate: Intens. raṃramyate, raṃranti, raṃramīti (Ved. rārandhi, according to Sāy. = ramasva, cf. Pāṇ. VI. 4, 103); [cf. Zend [ram, rām-a, airi-ma;] Gr. [Greek:ἠρέμα, ἠρεμα-ῖο-ς,] [Greek:ἠρεμ-ία, ἡρεμ-έ-ω, ἠρεμίζω, ἔρη-μο-ς, ἐρημ-ία,] [Greek:ἐρημ-ό-ω, νω-λεμ-ές;] Goth. [rim-is;] Old Germ. [rawa, ruowa, rawen, resti, rastjan;] Angl. Sax. [rest, restan;] Lith. [ram-a-s, rom-u-s, rim-ti,] [ram-dy-ti;] Hib. [reamhain,] ‘pleasure.’]

definitions.text: Ram, Nagar is a small village in the Surajgarha block of Lakhisarai district, Bihar, India, coming under the Ram, Nagar Panchayath and situated 19 kilometers east of the district headquarters, Lakhisarai. It borders the Begusarai district and is near cities such as Lakhisarai, Begusarai, Jamalpur, and Barahiya. Notable features include temples like Thakurbari Bakarchak and Shiv Mandir Bhawanipur, and educational institutions like Rajkiya Madhya Vidyalay Mustafapur. The local language is Maithili, and nearby rivers include the Burhi Gandak and Balan.

data.text:
Agni is the Lord of the universe. He is incapable of being apprehended or described. Capable of going every where and present in all things he is the Creator of all beings. He lives in the hearts of all creatures, Gifted with great power, He is older than Rudra himself.

Verse:
जगत्पतिरनिर्देश्यः सर्वगः सर्वभावनः । हृच्छयः सर्वभूतानां ज्येष्ठो रुद्रादपि प्रभुः ॥
data.reference: Mahabharatha->Anushasana Parva->84.18

data.text:
Janamejaya! Agnivesha Muni was directly the son of Agni. He taught his guru's son Bharadwajnandana Drona the great weapon called Agni.

Actual Translation:
जनमेजय! अग्निवेश मुनि साक्षात् अग्निके पुत्र थे। उन्होंने अपने गुरुपुत्र भरद्वाजनन्दन द्रोणको उस आग्नेय नामक महान् अस्त्रकी शिक्षा दी ।। ४० ।।

Verse:
अग्नेस्तु जातः स मुनिस्ततो भरतसत्तम ।
भारद्वाजं तदाग्नेयं महास्त्रं प्रत्यपादयत् ।। ४० ।।

data.text:
Agni is the god of fire and the performer of sacrifices. He is Agnidev Brahmana. 12.

Actual Translation:
अग्निदेव यज्ञोंके होता और कर्ता हैं। वे अग्निदेव ब्राह्मण हैं ।। १२ ।।

Verse:
अग्निर्हि यज्ञानां होता कर्ता स चाग्निर्ब्रह्म ।। १२ ।।
data.reference: महाभारतम्->शान्तिपर्व->द्विचत्वारिंशदधिकत्रिशततमोऽध्यायः->12

data.text:
Agni is Brahman. He is Pashupati. He is Sarva. He is Rudra. He is Prajapati. It is wellknown that gold is the offspring of Agni.

Verse:
अग्निर्ब्रह्मा पशुपतिः शर्वो रुद्रः प्रजापतिः । अग्नेरपत्यमेतद्वै सुवर्णमिति धारणा ॥
data.reference: Mahabharatha->Anushasana Parva->85.55

data.text:
Agni (Manu's fifth son) is the primary deity through whom all spirits, including humans, make offerings of food to the spirits in various rituals.

Actual Translation:
मनुष्य आदि समस्त भूत-प्राणी सर्वदा भाँति-भाँतिके कर्मोंमें जिनके द्वारा सब भूतोंके लिये अन्नका अग्रभाग अर्पण करते हैं वे अग्रणी नामक अग्नि (मनुके पाँचवें पुत्र) कहलाते हैं ।। २२ ।।

Verse:
अग्रं यच्छन्ति भूतानां येन भूतानि नित्यदा ।
कर्मस्विह विचित्रेषु सोऽग्रणीर्वह्निरुच्यते ।। २२ ।।

data.text:
Agni is the incarnation of Brahma, Pashupati, Sharva, Rudra, and Prajapati. It is believed that this Suvarna is the child of Agni.

Actual Translation:
अग्नि ही ब्रह्मा, पशुपति, शर्व, रुद्र और प्रजापतिरूप हैं। यह सुवर्ण अग्निकी ही संतान है—ऐसी सबकी मान्यता है ।। १४७ ।।

Verse:
अग्निर्ब्रह्मा पशुपतिः शर्वो रुद्रः प्रजापतिः ।
अग्नेरपत्यमेतद् वै सुवर्णमिति धारणा ।। १४७ ।।

data.text:
Agni is the preserver of this world, the ineffable, the all-pervading, the creator of all, the one who dwells in the hearts of all beings, the all-powerful, and the elder even to Rudra.

Actual Translation:
अग्निदेव इस जगत्‌के पालक, अनिर्वचनीय, सर्वव्यापी, सबके उत्पादक, समस्त प्राणियोंके हृदयमें शयन करनेवाले, सर्वसमर्थ तथा रुद्रसे भी ज्येष्ठ हैं ।।

Verse:
जगत्पतिरनिर्देश्यः सर्वगः सर्वभावनः ।
हृच्छयः सर्वभूतानां ज्येष्ठो रुद्रादपि प्रभुः ।। १७ ।।

data.text:
Agnivesha is a prominent student and compiler of the Charaka Samhita, a foundational text in Ayurveda. He is often depicted as a diligent learner who frequently questions his teachers, particularly Atreya and Punarvasu, on various medical topics such as the nature and treatment of diseases, dietary practices, and therapeutic procedures [1]. As a compiler, Agnivesha authored several chapters of the treatise, which were later revised by Caraka and Dridhabala, covering areas like the principles of Ayurveda, the treatment of specific ailments, and the preparation of medicinal formulations [2]. His contributions include sections on general principles, pathology, therapeutics, and pharmaceutics, reflecting his deep engagement with both theoretical and practical aspects of Ayurvedic medicine [3].

References:
[1] Charaka Samhita, Sutrasthana (Sutra Sthana) — General Principles, Chapter 4 - Six Hundred Purgative Preparations (virecana-ashraya)
[2] Charaka Samhita, Sutrasthana (Sutra Sthana) — General Principles, Chapter 10 - The (major) Fourfold Basic Factors in Therapeusis (Cikitsa)
[3] Charaka Samhita, Kalpasthana (Kalpa Sthana) — Section on Pharmaceutics, Chapter 1b - The Pharmaceutics of the Emetic nut (madana-kalpa)
data.reference: Dhara Summary

data.text:
Agni is the Vedic god of fire, serving as a messenger of the gods and often appearing alongside Yama in Rigveda (RV) passages [1]. He is also identified with Mars and described as the lord of eclipse cycles, playing a role in burning eclipse-demons to aid Indra in battle [2]. In addition, Agni is regarded as the Fire-god in Vedic tradition, having been revealed to the consciousness of Madhucchandā, who was thus enabled to sing the R.K.-songs; the text further notes that Agni is eternal and exists beyond human realization [3].

References:  
1. B. C. LAW VOLUME PART I, CHAPTER XXI YAMA IN THE VEDA  
2. B. C. LAW VOLUME PART I, CHAPTER XXVIII VEDIC GODS  
3. B. C. LAW VOLUME PART I, CHAPTER L BRAHMANISM AND JAINISM
